split_reasoning: One activity: walking the premises and checking doors, windows and gates.

parts.text: Walk a patrol round of the premises, looking for signs of intrusion and checking doors, windows and gates are secure.
parts.type_reasoning: The work is walking the site and physically checking fixtures, away from a computer.

notes: A patrol round could be treated as a discrete item with a patrol log; coded PHYSICAL because the work itself is walking and hands-on checking.

split_reasoning: One activity: going to an alarm or disturbance and dealing with it on the spot.

parts.text: Go to the scene of an alarm or disturbance and investigate it.
parts.type_reasoning: The work is hands-on attendance and checking at the site, away from a computer.

notes: The written report after an incident is covered by 2134.

split_reasoning: Checking and authorizing people at an entrance is a live interaction, while observing traffic for suspicious activity can also occur without an individual waiting for service.

parts.text: Check and authorize an employee, visitor, or other person's entrance or departure.

parts.unit_reasoning: One person's access check is completed and communicated during the encounter.
parts.work_item: one entrance or departure checked and authorized or denied
parts.start: person presents themselves at the access point
parts.end: access decision is communicated and passage allowed or denied

parts.text: Observe entrance and departure traffic and flag a suspicious or unauthorized movement.

parts.unit_reasoning: A particular suspicious movement is the actionable item arising from surveillance.
parts.work_item: one suspicious entrance or departure identified and flagged
parts.start: guard observes movement suggesting an access or theft concern
parts.end: concern is flagged for security action

notes: The split and shares depend on whether the site separates access checks from surveillance.

split_reasoning: One activity: writing up the shift's events and incidents.

parts.text: Write a report of the shift's activities and any irregularities such as damage, theft or unauthorised persons.
parts.type_reasoning: Each report is a written document that supervisors and clients rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Reports are written one per shift or one per incident and handed over whole.
parts.work_item: one daily activity report or incident report
parts.start: shift ends or incident is dealt with and details are recalled from notes
parts.end: report submitted to supervisor or client
parts.checked_by: security supervisor and the client or site manager

split_reasoning: One activity: calling the emergency services.

parts.text: Call the police or fire department to report an emergency or unauthorised person.

parts.unit_reasoning: Each emergency is reported with one call or a short series of calls.
parts.work_item: one emergency call to police or fire dispatch
parts.start: guard decides the situation needs outside help
parts.checked_by: emergency dispatcher, and the supervisor who reviews the incident

notes: Very short item; could be viewed as part of incident response.

split_reasoning: One activity: being present among people on site.

parts.text: Walk among visitors, patrons or employees to keep order and protect property.
parts.type_reasoning: The work is presence on the floor, away from a computer, with nothing produced.

split_reasoning: One activity: handling telephone calls out of hours.

parts.text: Answer a call out of hours, take a message or give information to the caller.
parts.type_reasoning: The caller is on the line while the question is answered or message taken.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each call is handled and ended on its own.
parts.start: phone rings and guard picks up
parts.end: caller gets the information or the message is recorded and the call ends
parts.checked_by: caller, and the staff member who receives the message

split_reasoning: Two different activities joined by 'and': verbally warning people, and physically apprehending or evicting violators.

parts.text: Warn a person who is breaking a rule and ask them to stop.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the live confrontation and nothing checkable is produced.

parts.text: Apprehend or remove a violator from the premises, using force if needed.
parts.type_reasoning: Hands-on physical work away from a computer.

notes: Time shares are a judgment; force is rare.

split_reasoning: Operating screening equipment is one on-site screening activity, regardless of the detecting device used.

parts.text: Operate detecting devices to screen people for prohibited articles before entry.
parts.type_reasoning: Screening requires physical operation of equipment and handling of people or belongings at the checkpoint.

split_reasoning: One activity: transporting or accompanying a person.

parts.text: Drive or accompany a person to a destination, or provide personal protection.
parts.type_reasoning: Hands-on physical work (driving, escorting) away from a computer.

split_reasoning: One activity: checking and adjusting security equipment.

parts.text: Inspect and adjust security systems and equipment, such as locks, cameras and alarms, to confirm they work and have not been tampered with.
parts.type_reasoning: Hands-on checking of equipment away from a computer.

split_reasoning: Building controls may be monitored and adjusted at a computer or physically at the equipment, which are different work settings.

parts.text: Monitor building-system controls on a computer and adjust a setting when needed.

parts.work_item: one building-system control adjustment made through a computer

parts.end: setting is changed and the resulting status is checked

parts.text: Check and adjust building-system controls at the equipment.
parts.type_reasoning: This work requires the guard to attend and physically operate local controls.

parts.text: Lock the doors and gates of entrances and exits.
parts.type_reasoning: Hands-on physical work away from a computer.
